_about: PRO batch 25: era 2 (last 3) and era 3, The Prime (30-33).

scenarios.title: The Big Market Rumor
scenarios.text: A big-market club is rumored to want you next season. Your agent mentions it 'just so you know', and every reporter at your locker mentions it too.

choices.label: Let the rumor be a rumor
choices.result: Silence, and no comment to anyone. The rumor stays a rumor, and you stay focused on this season, mostly, and the reporters move on.

choices.label: Reassure your club
choices.result: Your own club hears it from you directly: you're happy here. The general manager thanks you, and the front office remembers.

choices.label: Kick like it's an audition
choices.result: Fuel, every single week: you kick like the big-market club is watching every practice, because it probably is, and your leg has never felt better.

scenarios.title: The Weather Delay
scenarios.text: A lightning delay in the second quarter, and the teams go to the locker rooms for three hours. Your leg is cold by the first hour and stiff by the second.

choices.label: Plan the warmup with the trainers
choices.result: A warmup plan, built with the trainers: bike, bands, a heat pack every thirty minutes. You walk out loose and ready when the lights come back on.

choices.label: Keep the unit laughing
choices.result: Card tricks, bad jokes and an impression of {coach}. The specialists laugh through the whole delay, and three hours pass like one.

choices.label: Rest in the locker room
choices.result: A towel over your eyes, a bench, and rest. You nap for an hour, and you're fresh, if a little stiff, when they call you back.

scenarios.title: The Players' Council
scenarios.text: The players form a leadership council after a rough season, eight players, and they vote you on. The first meeting is Monday, and there's already a list of problems.

choices.label: Commit to the council
choices.result: Every meeting, every follow-up, every hard conversation with management. The council fixes three real problems, and you lose a lot of sleep doing it.

choices.label: Bring data to every meeting
choices.result: Numbers, charts and dates to every single meeting. The coaches start listening to the council because of the data, and say so.

choices.label: Stay quiet on the council
choices.result: On the council, quietly, letting the others lead. You vote, you listen, and you're glad when the season ends and the meetings stop.

scenarios.title: The National List
scenarios.text: Your name is on the national list for the league's best kicker, and the team's PR staff has eleven interview requests on a whiteboard, color-coded by urgency.

choices.label: Do all eleven
choices.result: All eleven, in a week. Your face is everywhere, you say the same three things forty times, and you sleep badly.

choices.label: Pick three and do them well
choices.result: Three interviews, chosen carefully and done well. One of them becomes the definitive piece about you, the one people still quote.

choices.label: Do none and keep kicking
choices.result: None at all. You keep kicking, the PR staff sighs and erases the whiteboard, and the list says what it says without your help.

scenarios.title: The Skills Contest
scenarios.text: The league invites you to the long-distance contest at the all-star week: a stadium, a television audience, and nine of the strongest legs in the league.

choices.label: Train for it like a playoff
choices.result: Two weeks of training for one contest. You go, compete hard, and come home with a trophy shaped like a goalpost.

choices.label: Go for the fun
choices.result: The week, spent with kickers from every club: dinners, card games, stories. You finish fourth and have the best time of anyone.

choices.label: Decline and rest your leg
choices.result: A polite decline, and your leg gets a week of rest. The contest happens without you, and you watch it from your couch, cheering.

scenarios.title: A Coach Out of a Job
scenarios.text: The head coach is fired after a Monday team meeting, in front of everyone, with a two-sentence statement from the owner. That night, {coach}'s office lights are still on at eleven.

choices.label: Check on {coach}
choices.result: A knock on the lit office door at eleven. You talk for an hour about the head coach, the business and the next three weeks, and {coach} thanks you at the door.

choices.label: Steady the specialists
choices.result: The specialists, gathered the next morning: same routine, same standards, whoever the coach is. The week goes on, and the young players watch how you do it.

choices.label: Wait and see
choices.result: Head down, waiting to see who comes next. It's the business, and you've seen enough of it to know that worrying changes nothing, mostly.

scenarios.title: The General Manager's Nephew
scenarios.text: The new general manager is the owner's nephew, thirty-one years old, with a spreadsheet about kickers that he's very proud of. He wants to meet you on Friday.

choices.label: Teach him about kicking
choices.result: A polite meeting, and a gentle education: what the spreadsheet misses, what the film shows, what a kicker actually does. He takes notes, which surprises you.

choices.label: Let the work speak
choices.result: No meeting needed. You let your practices speak for you, and by midseason he quietly stops sending you spreadsheets about kickers.

choices.label: Invite him to practice
choices.result: An invitation to watch a special teams practice from the field. He holds a ball for you, badly, and leaves with a new respect for the job.

scenarios.title: Loyalty or the Paycheck
scenarios.text: Another club would pay you double, your agent says, with the offer in writing. This one gave you your first chance when nobody else would. The general manager is waiting for your call.

choices.label: Stay
choices.result: You stay. The club remembers it, the locker room remembers it, and so do you, every time you drive past the old stadium.

choices.label: Explore it
choices.result: Your agent explores the offer, fully and openly. You kick the season like a free agent, and the club starts calling more often.

choices.label: Ask your club to match
choices.result: Your club, asked to come closer to the other offer. They meet you partway, and you sign, a little richer and still at home.

scenarios.title: The Foundation
scenarios.text: Your charity foundation's director is spending more on galas than on kids: the books show a ballroom, a band and a photographer, and only two new programs all year.

choices.label: Replace the director
choices.result: A new director, hired by you after a hard conversation with the old one. You run the next year closely, and the programs double.

choices.label: Audit the books
choices.result: An outside audit, every line, with new rules on spending afterward. The director stays, chastened, and the money starts reaching kids.

choices.label: Trust the director
choices.result: The galas raise money too, you tell yourself, and you let it run. The next annual report is glossy and thin.

scenarios.title: Broke in Your Thirties
scenarios.text: The money's gone faster than the career. There's a mortgage, a family, a car payment, and maybe three seasons left in your leg, if you're very lucky.

choices.label: Make a hard plan
choices.result: An honest advisor and a hard plan: a smaller house, no new cars, a budget taped to the fridge. It hurts, and it works.

choices.label: Tell your family everything
choices.result: You tell your family everything at the kitchen table. It's the worst conversation of your life and the best one; nobody leaves.

choices.label: Kick for one more contract
choices.result: You decide to kick for one more contract like your family depends on it. It does, and every practice feels heavier.

scenarios.title: The Pension Meeting
scenarios.text: The players' union holds a meeting about pensions and retirement plans in a hotel conference room. Six players show up, and you're the youngest by four years.

choices.label: Go and take notes
choices.result: Notes on everything, for two hours. It's boring and important, and you understand your pension for the first time in your career.

choices.label: Bring twelve teammates next time
choices.result: Twelve teammates at the next meeting, recruited by you one at a time. The union rep looks at you like you've performed a miracle.

choices.label: Skip it
choices.result: Retirement feels far away, so you skip it. The six who went start a group chat, and you're not in it.

scenarios.title: The Coach Who Taught You
scenarios.text: Your high school coach is retiring after thirty-one years, and the school wants you to speak at the dinner. The gym will be full of people who knew you at fifteen.

choices.label: Speak from the heart
choices.result: What that coach did for you, said plainly to a full gym. They stand at the end, and your old coach can't look up from the table.

choices.label: Bring the current team
choices.result: The current high school team, invited to the dinner by you, in their jerseys. Your old coach sees the whole program in one room and laughs through tears.

choices.label: Send a letter to be read
choices.result: A letter, read aloud by the principal. It's lovely, and you wish, reading the reports, that you'd been there in person.

choices.label: Tell the story of the trust
choices.result: How that trust was earned, and how you had to earn it again later: you tell the whole story. Your old coach nods along to every part of it.
choices.lock_text: having earned a coach's trust before

scenarios.title: The Rookie Kicker You Mentor
scenarios.text: The club drafts a kicker in the fourth round and asks you to show the rookie how things work. Everybody in the building knows what that means, including the rookie.

choices.label: Teach him everything
choices.result: Everything, generously: the routines, the wind, the coaches' moods. He'll take your job someday, and he'll do it right, and he'll know who taught him.

choices.label: Teach him the basics
choices.result: The basics, taught well, and the rest kept for yourself. He learns fast anyway, and you notice him watching your routine from across the field.

choices.label: Leave it to the coaches
choices.result: The coaches can teach him, you decide, and you keep your distance all camp. The room notices, and so, unfortunately, does {coach}.

choices.label: Do it the way you've done it
choices.result: You've done this before, so you know what to teach and when: the routine in week one, the wind in week three, the nerves before his first game.
